one_line: A machine-readable, agent-facing protocol for nonprofit donation destinations.
what_it_does: Publishes giving.json declarations and WebMCP tools so agents can identify authorized nonprofit donation routes rather than guessing through opaque forms or aggregators.
leverage_rationale: Structured declarations and tools materially improve donation routing, recipient fidelity, and repeatability over UI scraping; the agent-facing protocol is central to the concept.
leverage_evidence: Pitch identifies a standard JSON donate-page format and WebMCP exposure.
Frames show Verified Giving Protocol 0.1 with canonical-location and purpose fields.
Frames show a nonprofit donation flow with amounts and destination-oriented messaging.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent protocol concept and donation-page walkthrough, but no submitted video metadata/transcript and limited evidence of complete end-to-end agent donation execution.
execution_evidence: Live demo is reported alive.
Three frame sheets show donation UI, protocol form, and technical inspection.
No transcript or explicit agent-completed donation is provided.
impact_rationale: Nonprofits and donors have a concrete problem: agents can route to intermediaries or fail on opaque forms; an authoritative domain-controlled declaration could preserve funds and donor relationships.
impact_evidence: About text describes intermediary risk, delayed disbursement, and unreadable cross-origin forms.
Frames show nonprofit campaign and donation amount interfaces.
creativity_rationale: Treating donation routing as a verifiable web protocol, with the nonprofit's own domain as authority, is a fresh and memorable application of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Verified Giving Protocol 0.1 interface visible in frames.
usability_note: The donation UI appears understandable; protocol adoption and verification details are less evidenced.
red_flags: No actual submitted video according to packet facts despite frame sheets.
End-to-end agent invocation and donation completion are not directly evidenced.
standouts: Addresses trust and destination integrity rather than merely automating a donate button.
Uses a nonprofit-controlled canonical declaration.
advance_reason: Strong, socially meaningful protocol concept with visible implementation surfaces; Stage 2 should verify agent invocation and end-to-end donation routing.

one_line: A zero-knowledge webmail client whose browser-decrypted state is usable by WebMCP agents.
what_it_does: Encrypts account and mail data client-side, relays opaque traffic, and exposes inbox summarization, drafting, and navigation tools to an agent in the unlocked browser.
leverage_rationale: Client-side WebMCP is fundamental: a server-side agent integration cannot read data without breaking the zero-knowledge architecture, while the browser agent can act on live decrypted state.
leverage_evidence: Transcript explicitly says traditional server-side MCP is impossible because servers are blind.
Transcript describes six page-registered tools, inbox summary, suspicious-mail flagging, draft reply, and human-facing navigation.
Video is 159 seconds and titled as a WebMCP demo.
execution_rationale: The transcript describes a coherent security architecture and multiple completed agent workflows, including summarization and saving a draft; the product scope appears unusually complete.
execution_evidence: Video transcript explains browser encryption, ciphertext relay, and TLS endpoints.
Transcript reports inbox summary, suspicious email handling, and draft reply completion.
Live demo and public repository are reported.
impact_rationale: Privacy-conscious custom-domain email users have a real need for modern webmail without server-readable content, and agent assistance adds practical value without centralizing keys.
impact_evidence: About text says the creator uses YOZZ as a daily driver for custom-domain email.
Transcript demonstrates inbox triage and drafting while preserving zero-knowledge properties.
creativity_rationale: The combination of zero-knowledge webmail and browser-local agent access resolves a genuine architectural constraint in a memorable way.
creativity_evidence: Untrusted-content marking and background tools show thoughtful agent interaction design.
usability_note: Three-pane mail UI and background operation appear designed for practical daily use; login/setup burden remains.
red_flags: Security claims would require independent cryptographic and transport verification.
Sensitive email actions require careful authorization boundaries.
standouts: WebMCP is architecturally indispensable, not decorative.
Demonstrates both read and draft workflows with untrusted-content signaling.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP fit with unusually strong narrated end-to-end evidence and a compelling privacy architecture.

leverage_rationale: Shared structured code, audio test results, comparison feedback, and persistent attempt history enable a repeatable agent creative loop that is difficult to manage through generic UI driving.

No transcript/video metadata.

impact_evidence: Reference-beat recreation is a clear creative workflow.

creativity_evidence: Automated multi-attempt loop from one prompt.
Version graph linking each attempt to its predecessor.
usability_note: Inspectability and persistence are promising; audio capture/browser compatibility may create friction.
red_flags: No submitted video or transcript.
Audio comparison quality and actual agent invocation are unverified in the packet.
standouts: Concrete creative feedback loop rather than one-shot generation.
Attempt lineage and saved versions make iteration inspectable.
advance_reason: Strong concept and meaningful WebMCP role; advance for live validation of audio comparison and autonomous iteration.

one_line: A marketplace where buyer and seller agents negotiate multidimensional deals before human confirmation.
what_it_does: Provides storefront and negotiation tools for price, quantity, add-ons, shipping, and coupons, enforcing budget/floor constraints and requiring a human final confirmation.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP enables two agents to share live storefront/cart/offer state and conduct structured multi-round negotiation; generic UI automation is materially less reliable for this stateful interaction.
leverage_evidence: About text describes buyer and seller tools registered on document.modelContext.
Multi-round negotiation covers price, quantity, freebies, shipping, and coupon stacking.
A Confirm dialog blocks purchase until the human approves.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent full-stack product, explicit single mutation path, economic constraints, and a human confirmation boundary; lack of video limits observed completeness.
execution_evidence: Live demo and public repository reported.
About text names Next.js frontend, Spring backend, database migrations, and OffersService.applyTurn.
Description states settled deals reach a human confirmation dialog and no purchase occurs before confirmation.
impact_rationale: Shoppers have a real desire to delegate tedious bargaining while retaining control; sellers can express flexible deal dimensions beyond fixed-price commerce.
impact_evidence: About text identifies haggling as the neglected part of delegated shopping.
95k+ product storefront and explicit buyer budget/seller floor constraints are described.
creativity_rationale: Agent-to-agent negotiation over a multidimensional deal, with human approval at the boundary, is a distinctive and ambitious commerce interaction.
creativity_evidence: Negotiates add-ons, shipping, and coupon combinations, not just price.

usability_note: Human confirmation and constraint handling are reassuring; negotiation outcomes may need clear explanation.
red_flags: No submitted video evidence.
Live multi-agent behavior and product-data authenticity require validation.
standouts: WebMCP changes the interaction model substantially.
Strong economic safety constraints and one mutation path.
advance_reason: One of the clearest transformative WebMCP concepts, with strong safety and architecture evidence.
